name: Northwest Ridge
approach: Same trailhead and trail as the standard scramble: from Twisp, drive Twisp River Road (Co. Rd 9114) west ~10-11 miles, then Buttermilk Creek Rd, East Buttermilk Creek Rd (FR-43), and spur FR-4300-500 to the West Fork Buttermilk Trailhead (~4,000 ft). Hike the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail about 7.5 miles and 3,600 ft to 7,480-ft Fish Creek Pass; unlike the standard route, do not descend to Star Lake — instead gain the ridge crest directly above the pass.

waypoints.name: West Fork Buttermilk Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Twisp, follow the Twisp River Road about 10.7 miles and turn left onto Buttermilk Creek Road, crossing the Twisp River. Stay left onto East Buttermilk Road (Forest Road 43) and follow it roughly 4 miles, then turn right onto the Road 500 spur and follow it about 2.7 miles to the West Fork Buttermilk Creek trailhead at road's end, about 4,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Star Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: Hike Trail #411 up the West Fork Buttermilk Creek, fording the creek several times and passing long stretches of blowdown, to the trail's high point at 7,480-ft Fish Creek Pass. Do not descend to Star Lake; leave the trail at the pass, gain the ridge crest directly above it, and follow the knife-edge northwest ridge to its steep, loose final few hundred feet and the summit.

descent_text: no published account gives how the first-ascent party or any repeat party descended this route. Options in the area are either downclimbing/rappelling the ridge back toward Fish Creek Pass on the loose rock encountered on the way up, or, if terrain and party skill allow, working across to the easier Southwest Spur/scramble line used by the standard route and walking off to Star Lake before returning to the pass. Because the rock is reported as loose, back up any rappel anchors and expect retreat to be slower and more involved than the ascent.
